# Results — Study 932 (Trust Yield) on the real pre-deal SPAC tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The rule: at each month-end,
buy every SPAC still in its pre-deal window quoted **below** its accrued trust value with
30-730 days left to the redemption deadline; execute at the **next** close (one lag,
15 bps one-way on NAV); hold to the deadline and **redeem at trust**. Never sell into the
market, never hold through the de-SPAC, no shorting anywhere (so no borrow leg). Every
position is raced **excess-of-cash** against BIL's total return over the identical window.
Pre-deal SPAC quotes are **unadjusted closes** read off each SPAC's successor ticker
(a $10 trust is a dollar quantity; a post-deal split would destroy it); the cash leg is
**total-return** (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`). As-of **2026-06-30**.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | SPACs | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| 31 hardcoded 2019-2022-vintage SPACs (unadjusted pre-deal closes) | 2019-03-27 → 2024-04-10 | 31 listed, 31 with a usable window, **25 ever below trust** | `7d2c2f7b9919` |
| BIL (total-return cash leg; SGOV and ^IRX also loaded) | to 2026-06-30 | — | `b9dc0d8fa0bf` |

Bad pre-deal prints replaced by the previous good quote: **20, all in CXAI** (a March-April
2023 vendor artefact quoting a redeemable trust share at $1.33). Dropping that name
entirely *raises* the headline, so the cleaning is not doing the work.

**Hardcoded assumptions in force** (all swept below): trust at IPO **$10.00**/share,
redemption deadline = deal close − **30 days**, trust fee/tax drag **0 bp**, deep-quote
guard **12%**, cost **15 bps** one-way.

## The headline — buy below trust, redeem at the deadline

203 positions across **25** SPACs, mean holding period **302 days**.

| | |
|---|--:|
| Mean discount to trust at entry | **+1.47%** |
| Mean implied yield-to-redemption at entry | **+4.03%** |
| **Mean excess over cash, per position** | **+1.34%** |
| Hit rate | **93.1%** |
| One-sample *t* (positions) | +17.87 |
| HAC *t* (positions) | +17.96 |
| **Cluster bootstrap over 25 SPACs, 95% CI** | **[+1.04%, +1.63%]**, share < 0 = **0.0%** |

- **One position per SPAC** (the near-independent read, n = 25, first below-trust month-end
  only): mean excess **+1.45%**, *t* = **+7.46**, CI **[+1.09%, +1.83%]**, hit rate **100%**.
- **Redeem-or-sell upper bound** (take the better of trust and the deadline-day quote):
  mean excess **+10.99%**, CI [+4.66%, +18.02%]. Redeeming unconditionally throws away
  every deal premium on offer; the honest headline is the lower, redeem-always number.

### Read that table twice: it is an identity, not a measurement

With the payoff **imposed** at the accrued trust and the benchmark the same cash leg the
trust is assumed to accrue at, the position excess collapses algebraically to

```
excess  =  (1 + cash_ret) x (trust at signal / cost-loaded entry price - 1)
```

which `verify.py` confirms on the tape: residual **3.3e-04** across all 203 positions,
correlation with the entry discount **0.9992**. So **+1.34%, 93.1%, *t* = +17.9 and the
cluster CI are all statistics about the entry discount** — about how reliably a discount
selected on Monday was still there on Tuesday. **Not one of them is evidence that the
redemption paid**, because the redemption is a model assumption, not a measured outcome.
The one-per-name *t* of +7.46 is the same identity with fewer observations.

That is not a defect of the trade — a redemption right *is* a contractual identity — but it
means the study has to earn the Signal stamp somewhere else. Three real-tape reads do that
work, and they are the ones the verdict leans on:

**(a) Did the market agree with our trust line?** The deadline-day *quote* against the
assumed accrued trust, one row per shell:

| | |
|---|--:|
| Median gap (quote − assumed trust) | **+0.68%** |
| Shells quoting at or above the assumed line | **14 / 25** |
| Shells within ±2% of it | **14 / 25** |
| Worst shell | **−2.87%** (ALTI) |
| Mean shortfall on the 11 shells below the line | **−0.81%** |

No shell's quote fell more than 2.9% under the assumed line. The $10.00-accreted-at-BIL
trust is roughly where the market itself was on the day the put expired.

**(b) The assumption-free version:** *sell* into that deadline quote instead of redeeming,
so nothing about the trust enters the payoff at all. Mean excess **+10.43%** (*t* = +8.49,
cluster CI [+3.96%, +17.70%]); one per name, **+10.99%**, *t* = **+2.54**, CI
[+4.05%, +19.88%], hit **80%**. That clears the desk's |*t*| ≥ 2 bar without any trust
assumption — but it is a *different and far wilder* trade (its return is de-SPAC hype:
BFLY's shell quoted +100% over trust on the deadline, ASTS and MVST +28%), which is why it
is a corroboration and not the headline.

**(c) The adversarial payoff:** let the tape veto the $10.00 assumption name by name — pay
the **worse** of the assumed accrued trust and the deadline-day quote (`market_floor=True`).
This is deliberately too harsh, since the redemption right pays trust whatever the screen
says:

| Cut | n | Mean excess | *t* | Cluster CI | Hit | Book exCAGR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| All positions | 203 | **+0.83%** | +9.29 | [+0.28%, +1.28%] | 78% | +0.86% |
| One per SPAC | 25 | **+1.09%** | +5.40 | [+0.70%, +1.47%] | 80% | +0.60% |

The edge survives the harshest available haircut on its own load-bearing assumption, at
roughly two thirds of its size.

### The annualised number, stated three ways

The mean of the *per-position annualised* excess is **+2.31%** and it is the wrong number to
quote as a rate of return: it over-weights short holds (shortest quartile averages +4.40%
annualised, longest +1.20%, and dropping the 30-day floor sends it to +112%). The honest
readings:

| | |
|---|--:|
| Mean position (+1.34%) annualised over its 302-day hold | **+1.62%/yr** |
| **The book** — equal-weighted across open positions, net of cost, excess-of-cash CAGR | **+1.23%/yr** |
| Same book under the adversarial `market_floor` payoff | **+0.86%/yr** |

**+1.23%/yr over bills is the bankable figure**, not +2.31%.

### Look-ahead, named

The horizon filter (30-730 days to the deadline) and the deadline itself are built from the
**realised** deal-close date, which no one knew at entry. Lifting the cap to 3000 days moves
nothing — n 203 → 218, excess +1.34% → +1.36%, CI [+1.06%, +1.63%] — so the look-ahead is
present but inert. (In practice the *charter* deadline, which was known ex ante, is what a
holder would have redeemed against.)

## The two daily books (excess-of-cash)

Both books are **net of the 15 bps entry cost** (the cost basis is the grossed-up fill, not
the raw one — an earlier build valued them off the raw fill, which made the reported exCAGR
a silently gross number that did not move at all across the cost sweep; a regression test
now pins it).

| Book | exSharpe | exCAGR | Vol | Max DD | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Accrual** (hold-to-redemption) | +5.49 | **+1.23%** | 0.22% | −0.24% | +13.25 |
| **Mark-to-market** | +0.36 | +6.91% | 37.34% | **−41.20%** | +0.95 |

The accrual Sharpe of +5.5 is an **artefact of the construction**, not a claim: once a
position is entered, the pull to trust is deterministic, so the "vol" is only the changing
mix of open positions. The mark-to-market book is what a statement would have shown, and
its Sharpe CI is **[−0.31, +0.92]** (13.4% of resamples negative). Its 37% vol and −41%
drawdown come mostly from the modelled *forced redemption*: names that quoted a large deal
premium on the deadline day (OKLO's shell at $13.17, WEST at $11.04) are marked down to
trust on a single day. That is forgone upside recognised at once, not a loss.

## Robustness — era cut (entry year, split 2022)

| Era | n | SPACs | Mean discount | Excess (ann.) | *t* | Cluster CI | Hit |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2019-2021 (zero rates) | 124 | 24 | +1.40% | +1.25% (+1.98%) | +14.52 | [+0.98%, +1.52%] | 94% |
| 2022-2024 (hiking cycle) | 79 | 9 | +1.57% | +1.47% (+2.83%) | +10.80 | [+0.79%, +2.01%] | 92% |

Positive in **both** eras, with a wider discount and a shorter hold in the hiking era. The
late era rests on only **9** shells — the opportunity set was already collapsing.

|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | 203 | +1.49% | +19.88 | [+1.19%, +1.78%] | 95% | +1.39% |
| 15 bps (headline) | 203 | +1.34% | +17.87 | [+1.04%, +1.63%] | 93% | **+1.23%** |
| 50 bps | 203 | +0.98% | +13.16 | [+0.68%, +1.27%] | 82% | +0.84% |
| 100 bps | 203 | +0.47% | +6.40 | [+0.18%, +0.76%] | 65% | +0.30% |
| **200 bps** | 203 | **−0.52%** | −7.19 | [−0.81%, −0.24%] | 31% | **−0.78%** |

The cost never changes the signal (only the fill), so `n` is constant by construction.

**Trust value at IPO** — the single most load-bearing assumption:

| Trust at IPO | n | Excess / position | *t* | Cluster CI | Hit | Book exCAGR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| $9.90 | 130 | +0.83% | +10.51 | [+0.56%, +1.10%] | 83% | **+0.56%** |
| **$10.00** | 203 | +1.34% | +17.87 | [+1.04%, +1.63%] | 93% | **+1.23%** |
| $10.10 | 241 | +2.05% | +25.58 | [+1.69%, +2.40%] | 95% | +2.11% |
| $10.20 | 251 | +2.97% | +34.95 | [+2.60%, +3.33%] | 98% | +3.19% |

Note what a dime of trust does: it moves the whole result by more than the result itself.
The market's own answer to this question is the `market_floor` cut above (+0.86%/yr book).

**Redemption buffer** (deal close minus n days) and **trust fee drag**, per position with
the book exCAGR alongside:

| Buffer | Excess | *t* | Book | | Fee | Excess | *t* | Book |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 15 d | +1.31% | +17.58 | +1.22% | | 0 bp | +1.34% | +17.87 | +1.23% |
| 30 d | +1.34% | +17.87 | +1.23% | | 10 bp | +1.23% | +16.53 | +1.08% |
| 60 d | +1.41% | +18.46 | +1.33% | | 25 bp | +1.03% | +14.05 | +0.83% |
| 90 d | +1.42% | +18.07 | +1.38% | | | | | |

**Deep-quote guard** (6% / 12% / 25% / off): identical at **+1.34%** on all four settings —
once the CXAI prints are cleaned, **no** entry in the whole sample implied a discount
deeper than 6%. The guard never binds; the trade was always a small, patient one.

## Cross-checks

- **SGOV instead of BIL** as the cash and trust-accrual leg: excess **+1.42%** (+2.75% ann),
  *t* = +16.91, n = 179 (SGOV's 2020 inception shortens the sample).
- **Drop CXAI** (the only print-cleaned name): excess **+1.40%** (+2.40% ann), *t* = +18.28,
  n = 189. The result is not a cleaning artefact.

## The trust-yield path (median across live pre-deal SPACs)

| Window | Live shells | Median discount | Median implied YTR | 3-month bill |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2019 H2 | 1-3 | +1.5% to +2.3% | +1.6% to +2.1% | 1.5-2.0% |
| 2020 H2 - 2021 Q1 (the mania) | 8-16 | **−8% to −9%** (a *premium*) | negative | ~0.05% |
| 2021 H2 | 8-15 | +0.5% to +1.5% | +2.0% to +3.2% | ~0.04% |
| **2022 H2 (the peak)** | 5-7 | **+1.4% to +2.0%** | **+6.3% to +7.1%** | 2.3-4.3% |
| 2023 onward | 1-5 | negative, thin | n/m | 4.6-5.3% |

The trade only existed in the middle of that path. In the 2021 mania a pre-deal SPAC was a
lottery ticket priced *above* trust (median premium 8-9%), and by 2023 the pre-deal universe
in this list is down to one or two extended shells whose quotes carry a deal premium again.
The window in which a below-trust bill was on offer at a 6-7% yield-to-redemption is
essentially **mid-2021 to end-2022**.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

The null here has to break the *mechanism*, not shrink it: buying below a line and being
paid that line is arithmetic. So the null world is one where the trust put is a **fiction** —
quotes are an unanchored martingale walk accruing at the cash rate, and the terminal payoff
is simply the last quote.

| World | Mean excess (16 seeds) | sd | Naive position *t* > 2 | Cluster CI > 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Trust put binds | **+1.938%** | 0.144% | 16/16 | **16/16** |
| Trust put is a fiction (null) | **+0.002%** | 1.585% | **6/16** | **1/16** |

The detector recovers the plant every time and is dead-centred on the null. It also shows
why the position-level *t* must not be quoted: it false-fires on **6 of 16** null panels,
while the cluster bootstrap false-fires on **1 of 16** — right at its nominal 5%.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Real.** The discount was there; the trust line it was measured against was
  where the market itself was. Mean excess over cash of **+1.34%** per 302-day position,
  cluster-bootstrap CI **[+1.04%, +1.63%]** across 25 shells with **zero** negative
  resamples, positive in both eras, robust to the redemption buffer, the trust fee drag and
  the deep-quote guard. **But that headline is an identity** (§ "Read that table twice"),
  so the stamp rests on the three reads that are not: the deadline-day quote sat at or
  above the assumed trust in 14/25 shells and never more than 2.9% below it; the
  assumption-free sell-at-quote version clears |*t*| ≥ 2 on the one-per-name cut
  (*t* = +2.54); and under the adversarial `market_floor` payoff — the tape vetoing the
  $10.00 assumption shell by shell — the edge survives at **+0.83%** per position,
  CI [+0.28%, +1.28%], **+0.86%/yr** as a book. The mechanism is visible in the path too:
  the median implied yield-to-redemption ran to **+6-7%** in H2 2022 against a **2-4%**
  bill. **On the Signal axis, name the survivorship:** this is
  a list of 31 SPACs whose *successor ticker still trades* and which did *not* do a post-deal
  reverse split (the split names' pre-deal dollar tape is unrecoverable). Liquidations and
  delisted shells are absent. Because the modelled payoff is the trust — which liquidation
  also pays — the bias falls on the *opportunity set*, not the payoff; but the count of
  chances is flattered.
- **Tradability — Fragile.** The edge is real and tiny. It is **+1.2% a year over T-bills**
  as a book (**not** the +2.31% the mean-of-annualised column shows) for a 302-day lock-up in
  a $200-300m shell whose common often traded well under $1m a day; a serious book would move
  the price it is trying to buy. It survives 100 bps of one-way
  friction (+0.30%/yr book) and dies at 200 bps (−0.78%/yr) — which is one to three cents of
  spread on a $9.80 quote, i.e. a plausible number in size. It rests on the **$10.00 trust
  assumption**: at $9.90 the book falls to **+0.56%/yr**, less than half.
  It assumes the deadline holds, when 2022-2023 was the
  era of serial extension votes. Redemption is an operational act — an election filed
  through a broker, not a market order — and the modelled unconditional redemption forfeits
  every deal premium (the redeem-or-sell bound is +11.0%, eight times larger). And the
  opportunity is **gone**: the live pre-deal count in this list falls from 16 in early 2021
  to 5 by end-2022 to 1 by 2024. This was a two-year window in a broken market, not a
  standing yield.
- **Not modelled anywhere:** tax (the discount capture is a short-term gain and the trust
  accrual is ordinary income); the sponsor-extension calendar; the broker's **voluntary
  corporate-action fee** on a redemption election (commonly $0-$100 a ticket, which on a
  small line is a bigger drag than the 15 bps entry cost and is *not* in the cost sweep,
  which charges only at entry); and the possibility that a broker declines to process the
  election at all.
